title: Firefighter I
summary: Entry-level structural firefighter skills: PPE, SCBA, hose, ladders, search, ventilation, water supply, fire attack, and emergency communications.

skills.title: PPE Readiness and Donning
skills.summary: Don complete structural PPE correctly, check interfaces, and be ready to go on air without skipping protection for speed.
skills.whyItMatters: Gear that is open, twisted, or incomplete is how firefighters get burned and inhale products of combustion on ‘ordinary’ jobs.
learningPoints: Complete ensemble: helmet, hood, coat, pants, boots, gloves, SCBA as assigned.
Interfaces (hood/collar, gloves/wrist, waist) matter as much as the clock.
Inspect for damage, moisture, and missing parts before the tones.
Speed comes from repetition of the correct sequence, not from skipping straps.
beforeYouDo: Use YOUR issued gear. Training gear should still be complete.
Know department donning standard and when SCBA is required.

terminology.meaning: Where two pieces of PPE meet — a common failure point.
PPE and SCBA complete enough to make the assigned interior or IDLH task.

safetyNotes: Damaged or contaminated gear is not a fashion problem — it is a barrier failure.
Do not store gear in living areas; follow department cancer-reduction practices.

drill.objective: Complete a correct PPE don and partner check without sacrificing interfaces for the clock.
drill.equipment: Issued structural PPE, SCBA as assigned, timer.
drill.setup: Start from a standard ready rack. Partner calls defects.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Name every interface and one common miss (open coat, hood gaps, glove wrists).
debrief: What would you reject on a partner?

15.title: 15-minute donning reps
15.instructions: Three full dons with partner check. Time the third only after two correct ones.
debrief: Did time improve after technique, or instead of it?

30.title: 30-minute ready circuit
30.instructions: Don, short work (stairs or hose pull), doff/reset, repeat. Include a damaged-gear inject.
debrief: How do we catch gear problems before the next call?

readinessQuestions.q: The most important part of fast donning is:
choices: A correct, complete sequence repeated until it is smooth
Leaving the coat open for ventilation
readinessQuestions.why: Incorrect gear is not a pass, no matter the time.

readinessQuestions.q: A hood gap at the collar is:
choices: An interface failure that can burn or expose you
Only a problem on wildland gear
readinessQuestions.why: Interfaces are the weak points.

readinessQuestions.q: If you find a torn moisture barrier during a check, you should:
choices: Follow department defective-PPE rules — do not make entry in failed gear
Tape it with electrical tape and go
Only tell the person who issued it next month
readinessQuestions.why: Failed PPE is an OOS problem.

skills.title: SCBA Operations
skills.summary: Don and work on air, manage consumption, handle emergencies, and leave with a reserve — air is a tactical resource.
skills.whyItMatters: Most Maydays have an air problem attached. SCBA skill is survival, not just a test station.
learningPoints: Don, seal, and check before you need the pack in smoke.
Know remaining air, workload, location, and exit time together.
Emergency procedures are department- and manufacturer-specific — practice yours.
A low-air alarm is a decision point, not a surprise.
beforeYouDo: Use the assigned SCBA model.
Know cylinder rating vs actual work time — they are not the same.

terminology.meaning: Immediately dangerous to life or health atmosphere — SCBA territory.
The time/air decision to leave so you exit with reserve.

safetyNotes: Never disable alarms.
Buddy check the cylinder, valves, and connections.
Entanglement and regulator emergencies need practiced responses, not creativity in the smoke.

seeResources.label: SCBA Air Management Calculator
seeResources.note: Training estimates for work time and reserve.

drill.objective: Don SCBA, complete a partner check, work a short evolution, and practice the department low-air / emergency actions in a clear area.
drill.equipment: SCBA, full PPE, training area, radios, accountability tags as used.
drill.setup: No live fire required. Use reduced visibility only if the instructor controls the environment.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Buddy check: cylinder, valves, PASS, seal. State the low-air action.
debrief: When do we leave vs fight?

15.title: 15-minute work cycle
15.instructions: Don, short work, check gauges twice, exit on a simulated low-air. Time the exit walk.
debrief: Did work time match what you expected?

30.title: 30-minute emergency circuit
30.instructions: Low-air, reduced profile / entanglement talk-through, Mayday trigger criteria, and a controlled emergency breathing option per SOP.
debrief: What information goes in the Mayday?

readinessQuestions.q: Air management means:
choices: Using the cylinder until it is empty
Tracking consumption, location, work, team status, and exit reserve together
readinessQuestions.why: Air is part of the tactical clock.

readinessQuestions.q: A low-air alarm should:
choices: Be ignored if you can still see the fire
Trigger the department’s exit/emergency decision process
Always mean you have 15 minutes left
Be silenced as a first action
readinessQuestions.why: It is a decision point.

readinessQuestions.q: SCBA emergency procedures should come from:
choices: Your manufacturer instructions and department training
Whatever worked last year on another brand
readinessQuestions.why: Packs differ. Train yours.

skills.title: Hose Advancement
skills.summary: Deploy, charge, and advance an attack line as a team with nozzle control, communication, and a working backup firefighter.
skills.whyItMatters: Water at the right place, in a form you can still move, is the core engine-company product.
learningPoints: Flake to feed. A pretty horseshoe that cannot move is a failure.
Charged vs uncharged advances have different problems — train both if you use both.
Nozzle, backup, and officer (or acting) need the same picture.
Door control and stream selection are part of advancement, not extras.
beforeYouDo: Know the department’s standard line: diameter, length, nozzle type, target pressure.
Agree on who calls for water and who checks kinks.

terminology.meaning: Moves hose, manages slack/kinks, and supports the nozzle firefighter.
Getting air out and water to the nozzle before making the fire room.

safetyNotes: Do not stand in the bight.
A charged line can knock people down — body position and door control matter.
Know the stream’s reach and reaction before you open in a hallway.

seeResources.label: Hose Advancement Checklist
seeResources.note: Step review for deploy, charge, advance.

practiceResources.label: Attack Line Calculator
practiceResources.note: Know the pressure behind the line.

drill.objective: Deploy the standard attack line to a simulated entry point, charge, bleed, advance a short distance, and reset.
drill.equipment: Attack line, nozzle, engine or hydrant/training water, PPE, radios.
drill.setup: Mark a doorway. Assign nozzle, backup, and operator. Safety for charged-line movement.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Walk the pull, flake, and ‘ready for water’ report without charging if needed.
debrief: Who checks the first kink?

15.title: 15-minute charged advance
15.instructions: Pull, charge, bleed, hit a target, advance 25–50 ft, recover.
commonMistakes: Opening before the backup is set
debrief: What would we do at a real door?

30.title: 30-minute company evolution
30.instructions: Two-line or long-advance scenario: stairs or around an apparatus, communication with the pump operator, then reload for a true reset.
commonMistakes: Leaving a rats nest for the next crew
debrief: Did the operator know when we opened?

readinessQuestions.q: The backup firefighter’s primary job during advancement is:
choices: Feed hose, manage slack/kinks, and support the nozzle
readinessQuestions.why: The nozzle cannot fight the fire and the hose at the same time.

readinessQuestions.q: You should call for water:
choices: After you are already in the fire room with a dry line
When the line is flaked to feed and the team is ready per department practice
readinessQuestions.why: Ready-for-water is a crew condition, not a panic.

readinessQuestions.q: A charged line that cannot advance is often caused by:
choices: Kinks, poor flake, or no backup managing the drag
A hydrant that is too close
readinessQuestions.why: Hose management is the skill.

skills.title: Ground Ladders
skills.summary: Select, carry, raise, place, and climb a ground ladder for a stated objective: access, rescue, ventilation, or egress.
skills.whyItMatters: A ladder in the right place is a firefighter’s second staircase. A ladder in the wrong place is a trip hazard that helps no one.
learningPoints: Objective first: rescue, ingress, egress, or ventilation changes placement.
Tip, heel, angle, and locking devices are not optional.
Climbing with tools requires a plan for three points of contact and tool control.
Inspect before and after — bent fly sections lie.
beforeYouDo: Know the lengths on YOUR rig and what each is for.
Spot overhead wires every raise.

terminology.meaning: Moving and base sections of an extension ladder.
The base — footing and placement start here.

safetyNotes: Electrical contact can kill. Look up.
Do not overreach from the ladder.
Footing on ice, gravel, and slope needs a plan.

drill.objective: Given an objective, select and place the correct department ladder, raise, make the climb, and recover.
drill.equipment: Department ground ladders, PPE, helmets, spotter, cones or a building face.
drill.setup: Clear overhead hazards. Assign tip and heel. State the objective before the raise.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Match three objectives to three ladder choices on your rig.
debrief: Why not the roof ladder here?

15.title: 15-minute raise
15.instructions: Carry, raise, extend, set hooks/locks, climb to a mark, recover.
debrief: Could a victim come down this?

30.title: 30-minute objective circuit
30.instructions: Three placements: window rescue, roof access, and secondary egress. Time is secondary to correct placement.
debrief: Which placement would you change on a real building?

readinessQuestions.q: Before raising any ladder, a required visual is:
readinessQuestions.why: Look up.

readinessQuestions.q: Ladder selection should start with:
choices: The objective: access, rescue, ventilation, or egress
readinessQuestions.why: Length and type follow the job.

readinessQuestions.q: Climbing a ladder that is not locked/tied per department practice is:
readinessQuestions.why: Unsecured ladders move when you need them most.

officialSources.label: National Fire Academy
officialSources.scope: Free federal fire-service training and professional development

officialSources.label: Department ladder SOP and ladder manufacturer inspection guidance
officialSources.scope: Raise methods, tying, and inspection intervals are local and manufacturer-specific.

skills.title: Forcible Entry
skills.summary: Read the door, pick tools, control the door after it opens, and force only as much as the objective requires.
skills.whyItMatters: The door is both an obstacle and a flow-path control device. How you force it changes the fire.
learningPoints: Inward vs outward, metal vs wood, and multiple locks change the plan.
Gap, set, force — with door control as part of the plan.
Through-the-lock is a skill, not a slogan.
The objective might be search, attack, or ventilation — that changes how wide you open.
beforeYouDo: Irons or the department’s assigned FE tools.
A training door if possible; otherwise a walk-through on a real (non-damage) door construction.

terminology.meaning: Create a purchase, set the tool, then apply force.
Managing the opening so you control flow path and entry.

safetyNotes: Tools bounce. Eye protection and body position.
Do not force utilities or the wrong occupancy.
Glass and security bars are extra hazards.

drill.objective: Size up a door, state the plan, and complete conventional force on a training door — including door control after it opens.
drill.equipment: Training door, irons or assigned tools, PPE, eye protection.
drill.setup: If no prop, walk real doors and dry-run tool placement without damage.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Identify swing, likely locks, and first tool for three door photos or real doors.
commonMistakes: Hitting the knob first every time
debrief: What is our door-control plan?

15.title: 15-minute force
15.instructions: Gap-set-force reps with rotating roles. Control the door after it opens.
debrief: Would we have vented the fire by accident?

30.title: 30-minute FE problem set
30.instructions: Metal door, inward wood, and a ‘through the lock’ talk-through. Include a failed first attempt and a tool change.
commonMistakes: Destroying the door past the objective
debrief: When do we go to a window instead?

readinessQuestions.q: After the door is forced, a critical next thought is:
choices: Door control and what the opening does to the fire
Drop the irons in the yard
Turn on a fan immediately always
readinessQuestions.why: You just changed the building’s ventilation.

readinessQuestions.q: Forcible entry size-up starts with:
choices: Door swing, construction, locks, and the assignment
Waiting for a truck company even when you are the truck
readinessQuestions.why: Read the door.

readinessQuestions.q: Using more destruction than the objective needs:
choices: Can delay the job, create hazards, and worsen flow path
Is required by NFPA in all cases
readinessQuestions.why: Force to the objective.

skills.title: Primary Search
skills.summary: Search with team integrity, orientation, a purpose, and a way out — then communicate what you found or did not find.
skills.whyItMatters: Search is a life-saving assignment that also kills firefighters who lose the wall, the partner, or the exit.
learningPoints: Stay oriented: wall, hose, thermal imager per department, and a partner.
The search pattern should match the occupancy and the fire location.
Victim removal is a different skill from locating — plan the path out.
A ‘clear’ room is a report, not a hope.
beforeYouDo: SCBA, radio, light, tool, TIC if issued.
Know the entry point and the fire location as you understand it.

terminology.meaning: Maintaining a known reference (wall, hose, partner) so you can leave.
Rapid search for savable lives given current conditions — not a leisurely inventory.

safetyNotes: Do not search above an uncontrolled fire without a plan.
Holes in floors, wires, and collapse are search problems.
If you cannot find the exit, that is a Mayday problem — early.

seeResources.label: Search and Rescue Size-Up
seeResources.note: Organize search factors before you enter.

drill.objective: Complete an oriented primary search in a controlled environment, locate a training victim or a ‘clear,’ and exit as a team.
drill.equipment: SCBA, PPE, search line or hose as used, dummy or object, radios, optional TIC.
drill.setup: Use a training maze, darkened bay, or furnished room with instructor control. Set a time and air check.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: State pattern, team jobs, and Mayday triggers for a one-story bedroom search.
debrief: What do we say if we find a victim?

15.title: 15-minute search
15.instructions: Enter, search two rooms, maintain contact, exit. Debrief orientation mistakes.
debrief: Where did we get disoriented?

30.title: 30-minute search + removal
30.instructions: Find a dummy, choose a removal method, and get to the door. Include a lost-exit inject that is stopped before it is unsafe.
debrief: Would we have called a Mayday soon enough?

readinessQuestions.q: Losing contact with your partner during search is:
choices: A serious integrity failure — correct it immediately
Only a problem if there is fire
readinessQuestions.why: Team integrity is the search.

readinessQuestions.q: A primary search should be shaped by:
choices: Fire location, occupancy, access, staffing, and conditions
readinessQuestions.why: Search where savable lives are most likely, with a way out.

readinessQuestions.q: If you cannot find the exit and air is dropping:
choices: Treat it as an emergency — Mayday/self-rescue per SOP
Remove the mask to see better
readinessQuestions.why: Hope is not an orientation plan.

skills.title: Ventilation Support
skills.summary: Ventilation is a fire-behavior tool. Openings must match the attack, the search, and the chosen flow path — not habit.
skills.whyItMatters: Wrong ventilation makes the fire bigger, faster, and closer to people. Timing is the skill.
learningPoints: Horizontal and vertical ventilation have different effects and risks.
Coordinate with suppression and search. Uncoordinated holes are extra doors for the fire.
Know what you are trying to do: limited visibility, heat, victim, or fire travel.
Read smoke. If you cannot explain the opening, do not make it.
beforeYouDo: Know the fire location and the attack plan as briefed.
PPE/SCBA and fall protection as the assignment requires.

terminology.meaning: The route air and fire gases take from inlet to exhaust.
Openings in walls/windows rather than the roof.

safetyNotes: Roof operations need a sound roof, a ladder, and a reason.
Breaking glass injures people below.
Do not vent into a path that pushes fire over a search team.

drill.objective: Given a simple residential fire picture, choose whether, where, and when to ventilate, and coordinate it with a charged line.
drill.equipment: Building photos or a drill tower, charged line or tabletop, radios, ventilation tools as assigned.
drill.setup: No live fire required. Use FSRI-informed discussion: inlet, exhaust, and people.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Define the intended exhaust and who is on the line before any window comes out.
commonMistakes: Vent for ‘fresh air’ with no plan
debrief: Who can stop the opening?

15.title: 15-minute decision drill
15.instructions: Three photos: fire in a rear bedroom, basement, and kitchen. Pick openings and timing.
debrief: What smoke change would you expect?

30.title: 30-minute coordinated evolution
30.instructions: Line in place, then a horizontal opening on command. Debrief smoke/heat talk and a ‘too early’ inject.
debrief: Did we make it better for the search or worse?

readinessQuestions.q: Ventilation without coordination with suppression/search can:
choices: Create a flow path that grows the fire toward people
readinessQuestions.why: Openings are tactical.

readinessQuestions.q: The first question before making an opening is:
choices: Do I have the biggest saw?
What is the objective, and is water/search ready for the change?
Will it look good from the street?
Did someone already break the front window for no reason — should I copy?
readinessQuestions.why: Objective and timing.

readinessQuestions.q: Vertical ventilation is:
choices: A high-risk assignment that needs a sound roof, staffing, and a reason
The same as opening the front door
readinessQuestions.why: Roofs kill firefighters when the reason and the roof are wrong.

skills.title: Water Supply Support
skills.summary: Catch a hydrant, manage supply hose, and support the engine as assigned — the pump operator cannot do this alone.
skills.whyItMatters: Firefighter I water-supply work is how the engineer gets a chance to be good.
learningPoints: Know the department hydrant hookup from the ground person’s view.
Kinks, adapters, and a closed steamer cap are your problems.
Communicate when the hydrant is made — and when it is not.
Traffic and hose in the street are part of the skill.
beforeYouDo: Hydrant kit locations on the assigned engine.
Which outlet and hose the department wants first.

terminology.meaning: Hose from source to the pump, often LDH.
The firefighter making the hydrant while the engine spots.

safetyNotes: You are in the street. Visibility and traffic control.
Charging LDH can move violently.

seeResources.label: Hydrant Flow Calculator
seeResources.note: Why residual will matter to the operator you are supporting.

drill.objective: Complete a department hydrant catch, dress the hose, and report ‘water available’ with a meaning the operator shares.
drill.equipment: Hydrant kit, supply hose, engine or hydrant prop, PPE, traffic vests as required.
drill.setup: Use a training hydrant if live water is restricted. Agree on the radio words.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Lay out the kit and say the sequence including slow open.
debrief: What if the cap will not spin?

15.title: 15-minute catch
15.instructions: Drop, wrap or connect per SOP, charge on command, clear kinks, report.
debrief: Did the operator actually have water?

30.title: 30-minute engine support
30.instructions: Hydrant plus pulling the first attack line, then resetting both. Include a bad hydrant inject (cap, no water) and a move to a second hydrant talk-through.
debrief: When do we abandon this hydrant?

readinessQuestions.q: A hydrant firefighter should open the valve:
choices: In a controlled manner per SOP, after the connection is made and the operator is ready
Only after the fire is out
readinessQuestions.why: Controlled water prevents hammer and surprises.

readinessQuestions.q: If the hydrant is dry or broken, you should:
choices: Report immediately so the operator can change the plan
readinessQuestions.why: Early bad news is useful news.

readinessQuestions.q: Supply hose kinks:
choices: Can starve the pump just like a closed valve
readinessQuestions.why: Dress the line.

officialSources.scope: Free federal fire-service training and professional development

officialSources.label: Department water-supply SOP
officialSources.scope: Hydrant connections, LDH, and first-due hydrant programs are local.

skills.title: Fire Attack Fundamentals
skills.summary: Apply an effective stream as part of a team: the right stream, the right place, coordinated with ventilation and search.
skills.whyItMatters: Cooling fuel and controlling the flow path is how room-and-contents fires stay room-and-contents fires.
learningPoints: Direct, indirect, and combination streams are tools with reasons.
Gas cooling / hitting what you can see depends on conditions and training — follow department fire-dynamics doctrine.
A stream that never reaches the seat is noise.
Know when you are the attack line vs a backup/protection line.
beforeYouDo: Charged line, SCBA, a defined fire problem (prop, picture, or simulator).
Agreement on the attack mode the officer wants.

terminology.meaning: Where the bulk of the burning is — the target if you can reach it safely.
A second line protecting crew and egress, not a decoration.

safetyNotes: Steam, collapse, and flashover cues are more important than ‘getting a good hit’ on video.
Do not pass fire if your department’s tactic and staffing say otherwise.

practiceResources.label: Nozzle Reaction Calculator
practiceResources.note: Why the line is hard to hold.

drill.objective: Given a residential fire problem, state the stream objective, advance, apply water on command, and report the effect.
drill.equipment: Attack line, nozzle, pictures or a burn building if authorized, radios.
drill.setup: No unauthorized live fire. Use a simulator, photos, or an acquired-structure program under instructors.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: From a photo, name fire location, stream choice, and one condition that would stop interior attack.
debrief: What does dark turbulent smoke suggest to you?

15.title: 15-minute hit and report
15.instructions: Advance to a door, apply water to a target, give a conditions report.
commonMistakes: Opening the nozzle down the hallway forever
debrief: Did the smoke behave as we expected?

30.title: 30-minute coordinated attack
30.instructions: Line, a search assignment, and a ventilation decision. Debrief sequence.
performancePoints: Water before vent if that is the plan
debrief: Who owned the fire room?

readinessQuestions.q: An attack line that cannot reach the fire:
choices: Still counts if it is loud
Needs a better position, more hose, or a different tactic
Should be opened to ‘cool the hallway’ forever without a plan
Means you should drop the nozzle and search alone
readinessQuestions.why: The stream has to do work on the problem.

readinessQuestions.q: Fire attack should be coordinated with:
readinessQuestions.why: It is a company problem.

readinessQuestions.q: If conditions worsen when you open a door:
choices: Control the door, apply water as trained, and reassess — you may have changed the flow path
Vent the whole first floor immediately
readinessQuestions.why: The building will tell you.

skills.title: Communications and Mayday
skills.summary: Use the radio so people can help you: routine traffic, progress, and a Mayday that includes location, unit, and the problem.
skills.whyItMatters: A silent firefighter in trouble is a body recovery. A clear Mayday is a rescue problem with a chance.
learningPoints: Know the channel, how to key, and how to declare emergency traffic per SOP.
Mayday: who, what, where — and air/crew status if you can.
Practice before you need it. Stress shrinks vocabulary.
Routine radio discipline makes emergency radio possible.
beforeYouDo: Department Mayday policy and portable radio layout.
Your riding assignment name (Engine 1 backup, etc.).

terminology.meaning: Firefighter emergency — lost, trapped, injured, missing, or in imminent danger per department definition.
Priority radio, not the same as a Mayday in every system — know the difference locally.

safetyNotes: Do not wait until the last breath to call.
If you cannot talk, a PASS and a crew that notices your absence still matter — accountability is part of this skill.

drill.objective: Deliver a correct Mayday on a training channel, then a routine CAN report, using department format.
drill.equipment: Training radios or a timer and a written format card, PPE/SCBA optional for realism.
drill.setup: Use a training talkgroup. Never practice Mayday on a live dispatch channel.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Recite the department Mayday format from memory.
debrief: What channel?

15.title: 15-minute radio reps
15.instructions: Five Maydays from different locations (basement, floor 2 Charlie, yard). Crew acknowledges correctly.
debrief: Did location make sense to the RIT?

30.title: 30-minute scenario
30.instructions: Search evolution ends in a simulated lost-exit. Call the Mayday, then follow self-rescue/RIT talk-through per SOP.
debrief: What would RIT need that we did not give?

readinessQuestions.q: A Mayday should include at least:
choices: Who you are, what the problem is, and where you are — plus air/crew if you can
readinessQuestions.why: Rescuers cannot help a mystery.

readinessQuestions.q: You should call a Mayday:
choices: Only when the cylinder is empty
When you are lost, trapped, injured, or in imminent danger per SOP — early
Never if you are a probationary firefighter
readinessQuestions.why: Early Maydays are successful Maydays.

readinessQuestions.q: Practice Maydays belong on:
choices: The primary dispatch channel during dinner

skills.title: Overhaul and Salvage
skills.summary: Find hidden fire without destroying evidence or people, and protect property that the fire did not already take.
skills.whyItMatters: Rekindle, injuries during overhaul, and ruined belongings are preventable company failures.
learningPoints: Overhaul is still a hazardous atmosphere — respiratory protection per SOP.
Look for hidden fire with a purpose, not random demolition.
Salvage can happen during the fire, not only after.
Evidence and origin/cause need a thought before you toss the room.
beforeYouDo: TIC if issued, tools, salvage covers as carried, lighting.

terminology.meaning: Searching for and extinguishing hidden fire.
Protecting property from fire, smoke, and water.

safetyNotes: Holes, wiring, and remaining collapse risk.
Do not remove SCBA just because flames are gone if policy says the atmosphere is still bad.

drill.objective: Scan a room for overhaul hazards, open a designated void, and deploy a salvage cover or water-control method.
drill.equipment: Training room, TIC if available, salvage cover, pike pole, lighting.
drill.setup: Instructor marks ‘do not open’ evidence items.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: List five overhaul hazards before any opening.
debrief: When do we stay on air?

15.title: 15-minute salvage + scan
15.instructions: Cover a mock contents pile, then open one assigned void.
debrief: What did we preserve for investigation?

30.title: 30-minute overhaul problem
30.instructions: Hidden-fire hunt with a TIC talk-through, electrical hazard, and a rekindle checkpoint.
debrief: What would make us call the fire back?

readinessQuestions.q: Overhaul atmospheres:
choices: Are always safe when flames are gone
Can still be IDLH — follow department respiratory rules
readinessQuestions.why: Smoke and CO do not respect knockdown.

readinessQuestions.q: Salvage is:
choices: A firefighter skill that can run with attack
Always after the investigation is done, never during
readinessQuestions.why: Throwing water on someone’s remaining property without a cover is optional, not inevitable.

readinessQuestions.q: If you might be in the origin area:
choices: Minimize unnecessary disturbance and notify the officer/investigator path per SOP
readinessQuestions.why: Cause determination starts with what you did not destroy.
